subject: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike — Dedicated VPC timeouts (DNS/NAT) — urgent
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@finedge.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finedge.com
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx/429 rate hitting your dedicated endpoint

Hi Dylan,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx and 429 responses from our dedicated/private deployment using Redwood this morning at ~08:50 PDT. App-level errors and user timeouts are spiking — attached is a short sample of the server logs with timestamps (finedge-error-sample.log).

Pattern we see: client requests intermittently fail with 502/504 and a cluster of 429s following retries. Latency also climbs for successful calls (p50 -> p95 jump). We've already disabled non-essential retries on our side but the errors persist.

Can you confirm whether this is on the Redwood side or if it's something in the VPC/networking layer? We're on a Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with a private VPC peering connection to our account. This is impacting transactions — please treat as urgent.

Thanks,
Anna Li
Head of Platform
FinEdge

Attachments: finedge-error-sample.log (text, 36KB)

Hi Anna — thanks for the quick heads up and the log sample. I’m pulling in Sergio (network/infra lead) and Hannah (CS/ops) to triage right away.

Initial ask: can you share whether you see any recent changes on your side (eg firewall rules, NAT config, DNS changes) and a small pcap or tcpdump around 08:45–09:05 PDT? If you can attach a pcap we can correlate NAT and DNS behavior with our metrics.

We’re also going to surface metrics from the Dedicated pool (5xx rates, 429 counts, connection reset counts, and DNS lookup latencies). I’ll post updates in this thread as we have them.

—Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate hitting your dedicated endpoint — initial triage

Dylan / team — quick update from infra: we see a correlated spike in 5xx/429 from the Dedicated pool serving FinEdge starting 08:48 PDT. Key observations from our dashboards and packet traces:  

- 5xx rate increased ~18x for a 7-minute window; 429s followed as clients retried.
- DNAT/DNS failures: increased DNS query latency and some NXDOMAINs for internal resolver from the worker nodes (p95 DNS latency jumped to ~1.2s).
- TCP resets and TLS handshakes timing out from nodes to FinEdge VPC endpoints.
- Cloud provider telemetry shows ephemeral NAT port exhaustion on the service-side NAT gateway at ~08:47.

I pulled a packet capture from an affected worker and attached it (pcap-trace.zip). Initial hypothesis: combination of NAT port exhaustion (exposing SYN failures/timeouts) + DNS resolver timeouts cascading into higher client retries and 429s.

Immediate recommended actions:  
1) Ask FinEdge to share their NAT/firewall team logs — if they also have short-lived port allocation issues on their peered side we can have double-NAT contention.
2) Request CloudX (provider of our NAT) to confirm ephemeral port pool utilization and whether NAT timeouts were reported.
3) Implement temporary client-side retry backoff limits for affected route and enable local DNS caching to mitigate DNS tail latencies.

I’ve opened JIRA RDW-9871 and assigned to netops. Will update with CloudX response.

—Sergio
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pcap-trace.zip (pcap, 2.3MB)
From: CloudX Support <support@cloudx.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finedge.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-20T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Investigation — NAT ephemeral port saturation observed

Hi team — CloudX networking here. We correlated the timestamps you provided with our telemetry and observed a short-lived spike in ephemeral port utilization for the NAT gateway attached to Redwood’s service-subnet in us-west-2 between 08:46–08:51 PDT. Symptoms we saw match: SYN retransmits, connections falling back to TCP resets, and concurrent DNS requests timing out under load.

Root cause candidates:  
- Burst of connections from Redwood worker processes combined with aggressive retries from the client side leading to port table exhaustion.
- Firewall rule misconfiguration on the peered VPC that was intermittently dropping DNS responses under high connection churn.

Immediate remediations applied by CloudX (completed at 12:10 PDT):  
- Increased ephemeral port allocation for the NAT gateway serving your subnet.
- Increased TCP conntrack table timeouts to free ports faster.

We recommend Redwood reduce aggressive synchronous retries for the affected endpoint and enable local DNS caching / stub resolver TTL to avoid repeated lookups under pressure.

If you want, we can do an emergency peering firewall rule audit with FinEdge and Redwood engineers.

—CloudX Support

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-22T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary: NAT/DNS timeouts caused transient 5xx/429 spike — actions taken

Hi Anna / team — final update and summary for the incident (JIRA RDW-9871). Thank you for the pcap and logs — they were critical.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-06-20 08:46 PDT: Sudden burst of connection attempts from worker pool + client retries.
- 08:47–08:51 PDT: CloudX NAT ephemeral port allocation saturated causing SYN timeouts; DNS resolver p95 latency spiked concurrently.
- 08:51–09:05 PDT: Client retries increased 429 rates and application-level timeouts (observed 502/504s).

What we changed:
- CloudX: increased NAT ephemeral port pool and reduced conntrack TTL for the gateway.
- Redwood: rolled back aggressive synchronous retry policy for the affected route, enabled exponential backoff, and deployed a small DNS cache on workers to avoid repeated lookups during spikes.
- FinEdge/Redwood: scheduled joint firewall/peering rule audit for 2026-06-21 to remove packet drop points.

Result: error rates returned to baseline within ~20 minutes of CloudX mitigation + Redwood retry change. No data loss; no further customer-visible incidents after the 6/20 window.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Post-mortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/2026-06-20+FinEdge+NAT-DNS-Incident (will add timeline, signal graphs, and remediation owners).
- Netops (Sergio) to implement a monitoring alert specifically for ephemeral port utilization and high DNS p95 per pool.
- CS (Monica) to work with Anna on SLA credit scope if requested.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll share the full post-mortem and proposed roadmap items in RDW-9871.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
